subject: Re: Solaris scale negotiation — throughput proof & term proposal
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Erin Cole <erin@solarislabs.com>, Tom Becker <tom.becker@solarislabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Solaris: scale negotiation & benchmark kickoff

Hi Erin / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time last week. As discussed, Solaris is planning a staged capacity increase from 10k to 55k daily inference requests starting Jan 1. We’d like to propose a short mutual action plan to validate throughput and lock terms before your renewal window in March.

Proposed next steps:
- Redwood to run a controlled throughput proof with a 48-hour steady-state run (we’ll provide test harness and sample prompts).
- Solaris to provide representative traffic shape and 10 sample prompt archetypes.
- We’ll deliver a benchmark report (latency percentiles, token cost delta, KV cache hit rates) and a proposed term sheet with committed capacity pricing.

Attached: baseline SLA we would propose (solarislabs_SLA_v3.pdf). I’ve cc’d Marissa for pricing/term options and Karthik for ops/benchmark run coordination.

Can you confirm availability for the proof window the week of Nov 2? If not, suggest alternatives.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0183

Attachment: solarislabs_SLA_v3.pdf (PDF, 48KB)
From: Erin Cole <erin@solarislabs.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Becker <tom.becker@solarislabs.com>, procurement@solarislabs.com
Date: 2026-10-18T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Solaris: scale negotiation & benchmark kickoff

Hi Avery —

Thanks, that plan sounds reasonable. We can carve out a window the week of Nov 2 but need the following up front:
1) A short list of required test endpoints and authentication details; security will want the minimum scope.
2) Approx compute/network footprint so our infra team can schedule the traffic shaping.
3) A simple template for the mutual action plan / success criteria.

We’ll share representative prompts by Oct 22. Tom, can you confirm procurement’s preferred contract cadence (12 vs 24 months) — procurement@solarislabs.com on cc.

-Erin
Principal Product Manager | Solaris Labs

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Erin Cole <erin@solarislabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T11:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Solaris: scale negotiation & benchmark kickoff

Erin —

Appreciate the quick reply. We’ll provide the test harness (short-lived API key, sample payloads) and a 1-page success criteria doc by EOD Oct 21. Operational notes below for your infra team:
- Steady-state target: 55k requests/day simulated as 60k avg/day over 48 hours with peak bursts to 80k for short periods.
- Target p50/p95 latency: <= 120ms / <= 350ms for the majority of prompt archetypes.
- We’ll run on blazing-8 instances and enable prefix caching; expect approx 35% unit cost reduction vs cold runs.

Marissa will follow up on term options. Naomi (cc’d) will coordinate SOC2 & audit evidence in case procurement needs it.

If that all looks good I’ll lock the Nov 2 start and send the harness.

Thanks,
Avery
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Erin Cole <erin@solarislabs.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T09:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Solaris: throughput proof results and term proposal (draft)

Folks —

Following our internal dry-run last night, I’m sharing the draft benchmark sheet and a preliminary term proposal. Highlights:
- 48h steady-state (simulated): achieved 58k/day sustained with p95 = 310ms across the 10 archetypes. Attached is the raw CSV (throughput-benchmarks-2026-10.csv).
- With a 12-month committed capacity of 50k/day, the committed rate reduces token unit cost by ~22% vs current on-demand.
- We’re proposing a 12-month base + option to extend 12 months at fixed uplift; inclusion of automatic autoscale bursts (up to 80k/day) for an overage fee schedule.

Open items we recommend Solaris confirm before contract finalization:
- Final traffic profile (burst tolerance and dayparting).
- SOC2 evidence timing (Naomi to supply standard pack).
- Procurement’s decision on billing cadence and PO lead time.

Erin — can you confirm if Solaris wants the 24-month pricing sheet instead? I can attach both versions to the DocuSign packet once you confirm.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: throughput-benchmarks-2026-10.csv (CSV, 72KB)
From: Tom Becker <tom.becker@solarislabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-29T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Solaris: throughput proof results and term proposal (draft)

Marissa / team —

Solid work and thanks for the fast turnaround. The benchmark numbers look in line with our expectations. Procurement is ready to move forward on a 12-month committed contract with the autoscale burst addendum, contingent on: (1) SOC2 evidence delivered before signature, and (2) a short SLA edit to include an operational escalation path if p95 exceeds 400ms for two consecutive business days during peak season.

Please prepare a 12-month DocuSign with those conditions and I’ll route it internally. DocuSign link preferred — procurement requires signature flows tracked.

Erin and procurement@solarislabs.com are aligned on timeline to sign by Nov 12 if SOC2 evidence is available by Nov 5. Otherwise we need a 2-week grace for internal approvals.

Tom Becker
VP of Infrastructure | Solaris Labs
procurement@solarislabs.com
